blocks.value: **Order of precedence** is the set of rules specifying which operations are performed first in an expression containing more than one operator.
Some operators bind more tightly than others. Multiplication has higher precedence than addition:
`3` is multiplied by `8` first, then `10` is added to the product.
your handout's precedence table omits `^`, though it appears in the logical operators table. XOR binds more tightly than `&&`, which is where it sits above.
When operators of **equal** precedence appear in the same expression, all binary operators except assignment are evaluated **left to right**.
Precedence rules can be overridden with explicit parentheses, which group items and tell the computer which operations to perform first:
Same numbers, same operators, different results.

**Use parentheses even when you do not need them.** `(age >= 18) && (hasAccount || isAdmin)` is unambiguous to every reader. Relying on a reader to recall that `&&` outranks `||` is how bugs survive code review.
